title: Play-Nice Project Adoption Manifest
description: How a project consumes the shared contract library. Projects consume; they do not fork.

schema.description: Exact schema marker. Unknown values must fail clearly, never be silently reinterpreted.

repository.description: Repository identifier the library is consumed from, e.g. rylee-bee-labs/play-nice-contracts.

revision.description: Pinned revision (commit SHA preferred). Drift from this pin is reported as stale.

self.description: true only in the library's own .contracts/adoption.yaml: the library adopting itself. Checked by ancestry (the pin must be in the history being checked), because a commit cannot pin its own SHA.

profile.description: Optional profile name layered above universal contracts. A profile may raise but never lower universal floors.

always.description: Contracts loaded for every task in this project.

triggers.description: Surface tag -> contracts loaded when a task matches that surface.

requirements.description: Optional machine-checkable acceptance rules the project adds on top of contracts.

freshness.description: Optional remote-freshness policy. Absent means {policy: pinned, ref: main, update: review} (legacy behavior). policy: pinned keeps the reviewed revision authoritative; policy: require-current makes a verified authoritative remote revision a prerequisite of CONTRACT COMMITMENT: ACTIVE (fail closed on UNKNOWN/UNREACHABLE).

policy.description: pinned: existing behavior — the reviewed revision is authoritative for the consumer. require-current: the configured authoritative remote MUST be checked (git ls-remote) before mutating work.

ref.description: Authoritative branch the remote is checked against (branch name, not full ref). Ignored under policy: pinned.

update.description: review: a newer remote blocks mutation pending explicit adoption review. automatic: the pin may be refreshed automatically, but a fresh resolve/read/attest/commit cycle is still mandatory.

notes.description: Free-form context for humans and agents.
